price.label: Purchase price, land, building, fuel equipment and business
price.assumption: An assumed price for an older small-format store sold with its land, building and fuel equipment: about six times the illustrative FY2025 EBITDA, below the 9.3x median at which listed convenience operators traded in September 2026 [^32], since a single store has none of their scale. No asking price is cited, so that no real store at the exit can be identified; the going-concern appraisal and the business valuation set the value.

re_alloc.label: Price allocated to real estate (land, building, canopy, tanks)
re_alloc.assumption: 70% of the price. No published norm for splitting a station's going-concern value among land, building, equipment and goodwill was found; the going-concern appraisal sets the real split, and a lower real estate share raises the business portion that amortizes over 10 years.

inventory.label: Fuel and merchandise inventory bought at closing
inventory.assumption: About four weeks of the store's merchandise cost plus tank inventory for a small station; counted at closing and priced at cost.

working_capital.label: Working capital reserve
working_capital.assumption: Roughly one month of operating expenses, so the first fuel drop and payroll do not run through the line of credit.

closing.label: Closing costs: appraisal, business valuation, Phase I, legal
closing.assumption: A going-concern appraisal, an independent business valuation, a Phase I environmental site assessment with tank testing records, title and legal. The valuation and appraisal costs are buyer cash.

gallons.label: Fuel gallons sold
gallons.assumption: Below the 1.0 million gallons Yesway's older small-format stores averaged in 2025 on 10 dispensers [^28], because this store has fewer fueling positions and shorter hours than the 24-hour stores at the ramps. Year 1 carries the first full year of the QuikTrip that opened at Exit 62 in late 2025 [^11,12]; later years grow about 1.5% a year, near the 0.9% national vehicle-miles growth of 2025 plus local population growth [^35,1].

inside_sales.label: Inside sales (merchandise, beer, tobacco, food)
inside_sales.assumption: Below the $1.7 million Yesway reported for its legacy 3,400 square foot stores in 2025 [^28]; the subject's store is older, keeps shorter hours and has no food program. Grows about 2% a year.

labor_hours.label: Paid clerk hours per year
labor_hours.assumption: Two clerks on duty for 15 hours a day, every day. The store does not move to 24 hours; at these volumes the extra shift costs more than it earns.

wage_growth.label: Annual wage and cost growth
wage_growth.assumption: 3% a year, below the pace of the 23.3% rise in total store expenses NACS measured from 2021 to 2025 [^30].

burden.label: Payroll taxes and workers' compensation
burden.assumption: Employer payroll taxes and workers' compensation on clerk wages; no health plan for hourly staff.

manager.label: Store manager or owner-operator salary
manager.assumption: A market salary for the person who runs the store, charged even when the buyer works it, so EBITDA is not inflated by unpaid owner labor.

tax_rate.label: Property tax, share of appraised real estate value
tax_rate.assumption: A placeholder near the effective rate that full state, county, school and city levies produce on Alabama business property inside a city. No dated rate table or tax bill for the parcel was found, so the actual levy is a lender condition.

other_opex.label: Utilities, insurance, repairs, tank testing, card fees on inside sales, supplies
other_opex.assumption: Utilities for coolers, canopy lighting and HVAC; property and liability insurance; repairs; tank and line testing; card fees on inside sales; supplies and point-of-sale fees. Grows 3% a year.

seller_ebitda_fy2024.label: Seller EBITDA, FY2024 (illustrative)
seller_ebitda_fy2024.assumption: Illustrative. The research found no seller statements. Built from the same store economics as Year 1 below at higher volume (about 735,000 gallons and $1.08 million of inside sales) and 2025's fuel margin of over 40 cents [^30].

seller_ebitda_fy2025.label: Seller EBITDA, FY2025 (illustrative)
seller_ebitda_fy2025.assumption: Illustrative. Lower than FY2024 because large-format stores now operate at Exits 62 and 58 [^9,15]. It still predates the first full year of the QuikTrip that opened at Exit 62 in late 2025 [^12].

uses.label: Real estate: land, building, canopy and tanks (allocated)
uses.basis: Allocation of the price; appraisal to confirm

uses.label: Business assets: dispensers, store fixtures and goodwill (allocated)
uses.basis: Price less real estate; valuation to confirm

uses.label: Closing costs: appraisal, valuation, Phase I, legal
uses.basis: Due diligence for a change of ownership [^39]

opex.label: Property tax
opex.basis: Placeholder rate; tax bill is a condition
